findings.reason: a node dispatched against §10 must itself choose whether a lift may raise the utilisation ceiling (`lift-scope`, `data-choice=""` at line 1960, recommended `multiple-only`) and whether an unnamed-end lift stops at the next reset or after 12 h (`lift-default-end`, `data-choice=""` at line 1969), and unlike every other section, `§10` appears only in its own heading with no `/reckon-build … §10` prompt anywhere in the followups section, so nothing carries the invocation the chain expects.
findings.text: §10 is declared `implementable` to a node's brief, yet it carries two unlocked decisions that decide its mechanism and no followup routes to it

findings.reason: `/plan/<project>/<slug>` resolves to `docs/plans/<slug>.html` and `docs/plans/a-window-paces-the-lane-landed.html` does not exist (the record is `docs/evidence/archive/a-window-paces-the-lane-landed.html`), so all eight links 404 at the served plan and the section-by-section evidence trail cannot be reached.
findings.text: eight links into the landed evidence record use the plan route `/plan/reckon/a-window-paces-the-lane-landed#…` (lines 992, 1318, 1406, 1479, 1569, 1667, 1727, 1792) where the same record is addressed by the evidence route `/reckon/evidence/archive/a-window-paces-the-lane-landed` at 17 other sites

findings.reason: `_backends.budget_from_rate_limit_info` has parsed `unifiedWindows.five_hour` / `seven_day` since `b9562693f` (2026-09-05) and `b3977b3a7` (2026-09-15), both before §1's own "Measured 2026-09-21", and §5b's record at line 1862 names the pre-existing read path `_run_budget_probe → _backends.probe_budget → dialect.read_account_surface`; the premise is also propagated into `plan-summary` (line 10) and the §5 followup body (line 1993), and it is what §5's justification ("the reader shapes everything above it") and the duplicate-parser question §5b already raises both rest on.
findings.text: §1's load-bearing premise "Reckon reads neither" is false against code that predates the section and the evidence it cites

findings.reason: `BudgetConfig.slots` in `reckon/schema/flight.yaml` declares `drain_lead_hours` (line 690) and `pace_multiple` (line 702) and no `bookend_reserve_pct`, the model is `extra="forbid"` so an operator who writes the key is refused "Extra inputs are not permitted", and neither generated schema (`docs/_shared/flight.schema.json`, `reckon/_flight_schema.py`) contains it — while `reckon/crew/reserve.py:42,47,61` reads it with a hard-coded 20 % default, so the reserve §4 says is tunable is in practice fixed; §2 repaired exactly this class of defect for its own two keys, and §4 states the same claim without the repair.
findings.text: §4 records its landing as reading "a `bookend_reserve_pct` flight key from the budget block", but that key is not a settable flight key

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: finding — eight in-plan links address the landed record by the plan route instead of the evidence route, and that route does not resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §10's done-when is measurable (a named reading, a named lift, a named admit) and names a declared negative control ("deletes the lift lookup from `pace.policy` alone, and the admit assertion must fail"), which resolves on the real path because the admitted allowance is composed through `pace.allowance_for_group(…, config=config)` → `pace.policy(config)`; its `releases_at` expectation is derived from the fixture at assertion time rather than written down.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — evidence lives at durable repo and docs paths (`docs/evidence/archive/a-window-paces-the-lane-landed.html`, `reckon/crew/*.py`, `tests/test_*.py`), never a scratchpad or tmp path, and the mutation logs are named by scratch-copy provenance rather than a temporary path a later reader cannot resolve.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the landed modules (`pace.py`, `bar.py`, `reserve.py`, `hold.py`, `staleness.py`, `budget_group.py`, `pace_replay.py`, `window_reading.py`, `lane_document.py`) carry no plan labels, stage names, tool-verify numbers, version tags or changelog prose in symbols or comments.
rubric_items.reasoning: finding — the plan's stated starting premise is false against code that predates it, and §4 describes a flight key that is not declared, both of which a builder would act on.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable per node; each done section names one artefact (bar.py, reserve.py, window_reading.py, hold.py, pace rows, replay guards) and §10 names the lift alone.
rubric_items.wiring: finding — s10 is the only section not `done` (`implementable`), and it is the section with the least wiring: two decisions attached to it are unlocked and no followup routes to it, while the single `informs` edge is declared correctly.
